answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by tying earning power to counterparty-confirmed work receipts, not identity count. Like an opal that only reveals its fire under light, an agent gains weight only when a real counterparty confirms delivered work. Each receipt is non-transferable and tied to one task, so a garden of fake identities yields nothing, no counterparty vouches for work that never happened. An attacker must perform genuine work for many distinct counterparties, and that cost echoes across every identity they clone: copying the account multiplies the labor, not the reward.
